paragraphs.text: Turei Even, Megillah 2a, s.v. Megillah nikreis — “Why did the Mishnah not teach, ‘They read the Megillah on the eleventh,’ as it teaches later in the second chapter, ‘They do not read the Megillah’? One can answer that the times differ for different people: those of walled cities, towns and villages. One group’s time is not another’s, and not everyone reads on all these days. It therefore teaches, ‘The Megillah is read,’ since its reading does occur on all these days among different people. Still, perhaps the wording is not so exacting.” Turei Even offers the practical distinction between communities as an answer, while leaving room to question the precision of the formulation. Rav Tzadok instead develops its passive wording as an allusion to the light imparted from above.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Mishlei 9:2 — “What good name did Esther acquire for herself in this world and the world to come? All festivals are destined to cease, but the days of Purim never cease, as it says, ‘These days of Purim shall not pass from among the Jews.’ Rabbi Elazar said: The Day of Atonement too never ceases, as it says, ‘This shall be for you an everlasting statute, to atone for the children of Israel from all their sins once a year.’” The Midrash is expounding Esther’s enduring achievement through “She also set her table.” The maamar next asks how this can be reconciled with the permanence of every Torah commandment.

paragraphs.text: Shevuos 13a — “Could Yom Kippur atone only if one fasted on it, proclaimed it a holy convocation, and refrained from labor? From where do we know the case in which he did not fast, did not proclaim it a holy convocation, and performed labor? Scripture says, ‘It is a Day of Atonement’—in any case.” The sugya distinguishes the atoning force of the day from a person’s observance, while examining the different tannaitic positions. The maamar explicitly follows the opinion invoked by Rashba.

paragraphs.text: Responsa Rashba I:93 — “It appears to me that this means: Concerning all the festivals, He did not promise that sin would never cause their cessation at some time, as it says, ‘Hashem caused festival and Shabbos to be forgotten in Tzion.’ But concerning Purim He promised, ‘They shall not pass from among the Jews, and their remembrance shall not cease from their descendants.’ So too, ‘This shall be for you’ concerning Yom Kippur is a promise that it will be an everlasting statute: The day will atone even if they do not observe it. Rabbi’s view here follows his view in the Gemara that Yom Kippur atones for those who repent and those who do not. The ‘everlasting statute’ stated about Pesach, however, is a command rather than a promise: ‘You shall celebrate it as an everlasting statute,’ and, ‘You shall observe it throughout your generations.’” Rav Tzadok accepts Rashba’s distinction between promise and command, then asks what remains of Purim’s promise when coercion prevents its specific observances. His answer locates the promise in the enduring spiritual action of the days.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 21, 57b — “It is called Purim after Yom HaKippurim, for in the future they will delight in it and change it from affliction into delight.” The text actually names Purim after Yom HaKippurim and speaks of affliction transformed into delight. Rav Tzadok also brings the chassidic reading of Yom Kippur as “a day like Purim”; that reversal is his reported interpretation, rather than the literal wording of this passage.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Resisei Layla 22 — “Every festival, through a miracle and salvation, renewed an addition, and in the future ‘Hashem will be your light’ and there is no renewal; but the days of Purim are this very light.” Rav Tzadok there gives a second reason for Midrash Mishlei: the other festivals add holiness and so can lapse, while Purim adds nothing but reveals Yisrael's constant bond, and so cannot be nullified.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 18a — “If one read the Megillah by heart, he has not fulfilled his obligation. Rava said: This is learned through ‘remembrance’ and ‘remembrance.’ Here it says, ‘These days are remembered’; there, ‘Write this as a remembrance in a book.’ Just as there it is in a book, so here it must be in a book. Perhaps remembrance means merely inward reflection? ‘Remember’ could mean in the heart, but ‘Do not forget’ already addresses the heart. Thus ‘Remember’ means with the mouth.” The shared language joins the Megillah’s public oral reading from a written scroll with remembrance of Amalek. The maamar is attentive to the additional passive form “are remembered.”

paragraphs.text: Megillah 17a — “Is reading written here? It is performance that is written: ‘To perform these two days.’ Rather, the source is, ‘These days are remembered and performed’: remembrance is compared to performance. Just as performance cannot be in reverse order, so remembrance cannot be in reverse order.” Megillah 2b uses the same comparison to extend the distinction between the fourteenth and fifteenth from performance to reading. Rav Tzadok notes that these sugyos understand remembrance as the Megillah reading.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 20a — “From where do we learn the time for reading? Scripture says, ‘These days are remembered and performed’: by day, yes; at night, no. Does this refute Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who said one must read the Megillah at night and repeat it by day? The Mishnah is speaking about the daytime reading.” Megillah 20b again derives the validity of the entire day for the reading from this verse. The verse therefore governs the concrete act of reading as well as the meaning the maamar finds in the days themselves.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 29a — “‘I have been for them a small sanctuary’: Rabbi Yitzchak said: These are the synagogues and study halls in Bavel. Rabbi Elazar said: This is the house of our master in Bavel. Rabbi Elazar HaKappar taught: The synagogues and study halls in Bavel are destined to be fixed in Eretz Yisrael. If Tavor and Carmel, which came only for a time to learn Torah, were fixed in Eretz Yisrael, how much more these houses, in which Torah is read and spread.” The Gemara supplies the sanctuary status and future planting of diaspora Torah institutions. Rav Tzadok develops their present participation in the holiness of Eretz Yisrael through the Oral Torah.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzatto, Derekh Hashem IV, ch. 7 §6; ch. 8 §3 — “The root of all these matters is the order established by the supreme Wisdom: whenever a repair was accomplished and a great light shone at a particular time, then, when the cycle of that time returns, a light resembling the first light shines, and the result of that repair is renewed in those who received it. ... The purpose of Chanukah and Purim is to make shine the light that shines on those days, according to the repairs accomplished in them. ... Purim concerns Israel’s rescue in the Babylonian exile and the renewed acceptance of the Torah, which they accepted upon themselves again forever, as our Sages said: ‘They accepted it again in the days of Achashverosh.’ The details of these matters correspond to the details of the repair.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Ramchal describes the annual renewal of an accomplished spiritual change, and identifies Purim’s renewed light specifically with Israel’s rescue and acceptance of Torah. This clarifies Rav Tzadok’s claim that “the Jews had light” becomes active again each Purim. Rav Tzadok further develops that renewed Torah light as the holiness of Eretz Yisrael and the eradication of Amalek; those additional identifications are his own argument.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 11:7 — “Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Yosei bar Chalafta’s name: Avraham, of whom Shabbos observance is not written, inherited the world with a measure: ‘Arise, walk through the land, its length and breadth.’ But Yaakov, of whom Shabbos observance is written, ‘He encamped before the city’—he entered at the sun’s fading and set boundaries before day’s end—inherited the world without measure, as it says, ‘Your offspring will be like the dust of the earth.’” The contrast is expressly between what is recorded about the two patriarchs. p: And it is written in the Megillah,
to carry out the eradication of Amalek (Esther 8:16):
and gladness, and joy, and honor."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא
And this is according to what they said in the Pesikta
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק קַיָּים
"As long as the seed of Amalek exists,
the Name is not complete," etc.;
and this is derived from what is written (Shemos 17:16),
"For a hand is upon the throne of Kah."
וְהִנֵּה שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה אֵינוֹ נֶהְגֶּה [פְּסָחִים נ, א]
Now the Name Havayah is not pronounced (Pesachim 50a),
אַף שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז לְחָכְמָה וּבִינָה [זוה״ק ח״ג רמג, א]
although it alludes to Chochmah and Binah (Zohar III 243a),
but together with the vav-hei, which allude to the seven lower sefiros (ibid.),
But the essence of the union
as we say before every mitzvah,
"to unify the Name of yud-hei with vav-hei";
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and this is according to what they said in the holy Zohar
אִכְלוּ רֵעִים [שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ה, א] וְכוּלֵּי
who are in unity, in joy,
who are joined only at set times."
That is, the union of yud-hei is constant,
וְאוֹתִיּוֹת י״ה הוּא שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
And the letters yud-hei are a Name in themselves,
And this union one is able to merit:
that the wisdom in the mind be joined
with the understanding and the will in the heart.
אֲבָל הָעִיקָּר לְיַחֵד שֵׁם י״ה בְּו״ה
But the main thing is to unify the Name yud-hei with vav-hei,
so that the union be with Knesses Yisrael.
And the letters vav-hei allude to Torah and mitzvos,
as they said in the holy Zohar
and therefore the letters vav-hei by themselves
for Chochmah and Binah are hidden
in the mind and the heart,
and Torah without fear and love
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר (תִּקּוּן י כה, ב).
as they said in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 10, 25b).
And the essence of the union is to merit
that there be a union of the Name yud-hei with vav-hei,
that is, that there be the union
of Chochmah and Binah, mind and heart,
with the deed of Torah and mitzvos.
וְזֶה הַיִּחוּד לֹא יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת בִּשְׁלֵימוּת
And this union cannot be complete
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק קַיָּים
as long as the seed of Amalek exists;
that is, as long as Amalek has existence,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (ח״ג קס, א)
as they said in the holy Zohar (III 160a)
"Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev,"
and it is able to enter
even into the hearts of great and holy people
maamar 1; and see there at length).
Therefore, after the eradication of Amalek,
four things corresponding to the four letters
"Light" corresponds to the yud of the Name,
is the utterance "Let there be light" (Bereishis 1:3),
and "light" is written there five times,
corresponding to the five Chumashim of the Torah
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [יְשַׁעְיָה ו, י] וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין
as it says (Yeshayah 6:10), "and his heart will understand,"
וּכְתִיב [תְּהִלִּים צז, יא] וּלְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה
and it is written (Tehillim 97:11), "and gladness for the upright of heart";
that is, when the heart is made upright,
when one empties the evil from the heart of the fool
And likewise we find in the verses
that gladness is attributed to the heart:
יִשְׂמַח לֵב מְבַקְשֵׁי ה׳ [תְּהִלִּים קה, ג]
"Let the heart of those who seek Hashem be glad" (Tehillim 105:3);
וְכֵן נָתַתָּ שִׂמְחָה בְלִבִּי [שָׁם ד, ח]
and likewise, "You have put gladness in my heart" (ibid. 4:8);
יִשְׂמַח לִבִּי גַם אָנִי [מִשְׁלֵי כג, טו]
"my heart too will be glad, even mine" (Mishlei 23:15);
"Joy" corresponds to the vav in the Name Havayah,
which is "the river going out of Eden
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א׳ כו, א)
וּכְתִיב [יְשַׁעְיָה יב, ג] וּשְׁאַבְתֶּם מַיִם בְּשָׂשׂוֹן
and it is written (Yeshayah 12:3), "And you shall draw water with joy
that is, the river that flows and goes forth
וְאִיתָא בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי (סוּכָּה פ״ה ה״א כב, ב)
And it is stated in the Yerushalmi (Sukkah 5:1, 22b),
הוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת (סוּכָּה נ, ב ד״ה חַד)
that from there they drew ruach hakodesh;
and it is stated in the holy Zohar
a spirit from that holy one above";
that is, through the central pillar,
which goes out of Eden to water the garden,
"and joy" is expounded: "This is milah," etc.
And it is all one, for body and covenant
are counted as one, as they said
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ רמב ב וְשָׁאַר מְקוֹמוֹת)
"And the two of them go together,
and this is the secret of the letter vav-vav,
that both of them go together," etc.
That is, regarding Yaakov it is written (Michah 7:20),
אוֹת ו׳ דְּדָא אִיקְרֵי אוֹת אֱמֶת
the letter vav, for this is called "the letter of truth,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (ח״ג ב, א)
as they said in the holy Zohar (III 2a);
and Yosef is the small letter vav,
the vav of the spelled-out letter,
וְכֵן כָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם יא, א)
and so it is written in the holy Zohar (ibid. 11a).
Therefore it is stated in the holy Zohar
and it is stated (Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 24)
that he is "the tzaddik who goes forth from Eden," etc.;
"Honor" corresponds to the final hei of the Name;
and in the Gemara (Megillah, ibid.) they said,
and this is in the manner of what they said
the aspect of a crown upon the mind in their head;
and likewise "honor" is the aspect of Atika,
as has been explained many times,
And it corresponds to the hei, the lower Shechinah,
in the secret of "its end is embedded in its beginning."
And corresponding to the four things mentioned above,
there are four mitzvos on Purim:
similar to what they said (Megillah, ibid.)
And although the Megillah is rabbinic,
"We say that it was given to be written";
that is fixed in the heart for all generations,
שֶׁעַל זֶה מוֹרֶה מַה שֶּׁנִּיתַּן לִכְתּוֹב
which is indicated by its having been given to be written;
יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵּי
"Yaakov, regarding whom Shabbos observance is written," etc.:
אַף שֶׁגַּם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
although Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, also
as part of all the mitzvos that he kept,
that "it is not written regarding him," etc.;
but regarding Yaakov, of whom it is written explicitly,
that the holiness was fixed in him forever
And this is the matter of "light"
corresponding to the reading of the Megillah,
which contains the light that was given to be written.
And it corresponds to the yud in the Name Havayah.
And in the Yerushalmi (Megillah, perek 1, halachah 5)
it is stated: "Also Megillas Esther and the halachos
will not in the future be nullified;
נֶאֱמַר כָּאן [דְּבָרִים ה, יט] וְלֹא יָסָף
it says here (Devarim 5:19), 'and did not add,'
'nor shall their remembrance cease from their seed.'"
אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּבָּטְלוּ שְׁאָר הַנְּבִיאִים עַיֵּין שָׁם.
even of the time when the rest of the Prophets will be nullified; see there.
were said only to undo the "much anger,"
they would have been given only
the five Chumashim of the Torah," etc.,
"For in much wisdom is much anger."
This is not so of the Megillah,
that will shine in the heart,
and the light will be fixed in the heart forever,
and this will not be nullified.
And this is what they said, "The Megillah is read":
that is merited through reading the Megillah,
for the light comes from Hashem Yisbarach,
רַק עַל יְדֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹרִין לְמַטָּה.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק
similar to what they said about the eradication of Amalek,
and I erase his name from above."
And this hint comes at the beginning of the tractate,
for this is the whole essence of the matter
of the mitzvah of Purim and the reading of the Megillah:
and the light be fixed forever
And it teaches the power of the words of the Sofrim,
who granted power with regard to the villages:
that although they read on the eleventh,
אוֹ בִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר אוֹ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר
or the twelfth, or the thirteenth,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יִהְיוּ לָהֶם כֹּחַ זֶה
nevertheless they will have this power,
for it to be "read" from above,
and they will merit the light.
2) The mitzvah of feasting and rejoicing
corresponds to what is said, "and gladness,"
which corresponds to the upper hei,
Binah, the heart, as we said.
And it is written "feasting and gladness,"
that all forbidden relations seem to him like level ground
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יִשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי הַיַּיִן
so that it be entirely good,
that they be joyous and good-hearted;
and this is what they said (ibid. 76b),
"gladness for the upright of heart," as mentioned above.
And similar to what they said (Megillah 12b):
they begin with words of Torah
and words of praise; but," etc.
And as we saw at his feast,
where the vileness of his heart was revealed
even by the standards of idolaters.
And this is "If he does not merit, it desolates him":
that all forbidden relations seem to him like level ground,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [מִשְׁלֵי כג, לא] יִתְהַלֵּךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִים
as it says (Mishlei 23:31), "it goes down smoothly,"
as they said in the Gemara there (Yoma 75).
corresponds to what is said, "and joy,"
which corresponds to the vav in the Name,
together with the vav of the spelled-out letter, as we said.
And the root of the mitzvah is to unite the hearts,
that they be like one man with one heart;
and this is a preparation to receive the words of Torah,
as we find at Matan Torah,
where it is written (Shemos 19:2), "And Yisrael encamped"—
as they said in the Mechilta (Yisro, BaChodesh 1);
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
and through this they merited Matan Torah.
is through the river that flows and goes forth;
that is, when they merit the attribute of peace,
to be like one man with one heart,
through this they draw down the light,
which is the garden, the lower Shechinah.
And this is the holiness of Yaakov and Yosef:
the attribute of truth for Yaakov,
וְיוֹסֵף שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ שָׁלוֹם [זוה״ק ח״א קצז, ב]
and Yosef, whose attribute is peace (Zohar I 197b);
וּכְתִיב [זְכַרְיָה ח, יט] וְהָאֱמֶת וְהַשָּׁלוֹם אֱהָבוּ
and it is written (Zechariah 8:19), "Love truth and peace,"
for truth and peace are bound one to the other
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ יב, ב).
and to what is said, "and honor";
and this is according to what they said
[הַקְדָּמַת תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר בְּפֶתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ] צֶדֶק מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא.
(Introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, Pesach Eliyahu): "Tzedek is the holy Malchus."
And when it is complete, with the hei, it is tzedakah,
as they said in Tikkunei Zohar
וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בַּעַל צְדָקָה וְכוּלֵּי
and HaKadosh Baruch Hu the master of tzedakah, etc.;
For tzedek is the lower Shechinah,
and when it is drawn from Eden,
the upper Shechinah, it is tzedakah;
and this is what they said in Tikkunei Zohar (ibid.):
in the words of Torah—without limit;
וְכֵן כְּתִיב [תְּהִלִּים קיב, ט] קַרְנוֹ תָּרוּם בְּכָבוֹד
and likewise it is written (Tehillim 112:9), "His horn shall be exalted with honor,"
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא נֶגֶד מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר וִיקָר
Therefore it corresponds to what is said, "and honor,"
which indicates Atika, as mentioned above,
it is expounded as the tefillin of the head.
And it is written, "And these days
are remembered and kept in every generation":
that even should it come about, Heaven forbid,
the working of the power of the days,
and they will merit the union of the Name Havayah,
עַל יְדֵי הַיָּמִים הָאֵלֶּה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
through these days, as mentioned above.
And this will be through the remembrance
which also comes from Hashem Yisbarach,
"nor shall their remembrance cease from their seed."
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַיֵּים מִצְוֹתָיו תְּחִלָּה
And HaKadosh Baruch Hu fulfills His mitzvos first,
and even the mitzvos of the Elders
as they said in the Pesikta

In this world it is written with Yud–Heh and read with Alef–Dalet; in the world to come all is one: It is read with Yud–Heh and written with Yud–Heh.” The Gemara contrasts the written four-letter Name with its substituted pronunciation. paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 4a — “Rabbi Shimon said: ‘Eat, friends’ refers above; ‘Drink and become intoxicated, beloved ones’ refers below. The higher place is where they are in unity and joy, never separating; these are called friends. Eden and the river that flows from it never separate, but are forever in will, unity and joy. The beloved ones below unite at known times. Those who yearn for one another and are not always together are called beloved ones; those always present and never separating are called friends. Through this completeness the congregation of Israel is blessed and there is joy in all worlds.” The distinction is precisely between abiding union above and union at particular times below. Rav Tzadok applies it to Yud–Heh and their union with Vav–Heh.

Everyone who gives charity to a poor person causes the river to flow from Eden, the supernal Mother, to water the garden, the dalet, poor and needy. When she descends filled to her husband, Vav enters dalet and it becomes Heh. What was tzedek becomes tzedakah. Concerning that river it says, ‘Charity raises a nation’; what was tzedek, judgment, becomes mercy.” The addition of Heh to tzedek is described through giving, filling and mercy. Rav Tzadok reads the raising of a nation as ascent to the highest source, the preciousness signified by yekar.

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma, Naso 29; Pesikta Rabbati 3 — “A person should not say: I will not fulfill the elders’ commandments, since they are not from the Torah. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: My children, you may not speak so. Rather, fulfill everything they decree for you, as it says, ‘You shall act according to the instruction they teach you.’ For I too agree with their words, as it says, ‘You will decree a matter, and it will be established for you.’ Yaakov placed Ephraim before Menasheh, and the Holy One fulfilled his decree in the princes’ offerings: Ephraim offered first, then Menasheh.” Pesikta Rabbati 3 likewise concludes that Yaakov’s placing Ephraim first was honored in the offerings. The maamar extends this concurrence with the elders to the rabbinic mitzvos of Purim.

De’alach sani — “‘What is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow’: ‘Your friend and your father’s friend do not abandon’—this is the Holy One, blessed be He. Umitzvas mishloach manos — “The mitzvah of sending portions appears intended to bring one to love of Israel. ‘Love your fellow as yourself’ is a great principle in Torah. When a person cleaves to the inward point of life, where all Israel are one, he naturally loves his fellow too. This is itself what Rashi says, ‘Your friend is the Holy One,’ for all is one. Mordechai comprised all Israel: Through the love that makes them one, he could bring the merit of his deeds upon all Israel. He cleaved to the point of life where unity resides. My grandfather likewise explained ‘Israel encamped before the mountain’: Unity prepares for receiving Torah; here too, in Purim, there was acceptance of Torah.”

The maamar applies its spiritual counterpart to all who seek Hashem’s salvation.

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rambam explicitly places resemblance to the Shechinah within the mitzvah of Purim gifts: bringing life and gladness to the lowly is itself a divine action. This illuminates Rav Tzadok’s conclusion that God fulfills these gifts by giving to those who seek His rescue. The same mitzvah links human relief of poverty with the divine bestowal described in the maamar.
